title: Signal engine: development/historical walk-forward bootstrap (one-off, re-run weekly by a session if useful): for each of the last 7 complete days in the feature store, fit every non-embargoed model on data available before that day and score that day's captures in memory; written to dev/ and shown on /lab as 'development/historical', never pooled with prospective scores
expected_value: an honest development baseline while prospective scores accumulate (first 14 days)
next_action: promote once q0510 has backfilled the captures still on the host (>= 3 days); it re-writes dashboard.json with the development block
notes: Promoted 2026-10-21 by the signal-engine autopilot (signal engine v1, docs/research_lab/signal_engine/DESIGN_V1.md section 9). Measured on the host 2026-10-20 23:26-23:45Z in a read-only dry run (/tmp/sigeng, engine root outside ~/arepo, deleted afterwards). Each test day is one in-memory refit (measured 6.7-7.5 min / 1.07 GB at 385k rows; 200k rows here) plus in-memory prediction of 12 captures (~30 s each): expect ~40-60 min for 7 days. Embargoed challengers get no development scores either (their rows show only the embargo date). depends_on is empty on purpose: the other engine jobs are repeat jobs that never reach 'done'; missing inputs make this job exit 75 or report 'insufficient'/'no_fit' instead. 2026-10-21 14:10Z (signal-engine autopilot): first host run started 12:28Z with 3 non-embargoed models (se0 + two LightGBM, se1 and se7); a host LightGBM fit takes 8.5-10.5 min at 300k rows, so a test day is ~15 min and 7 days ~105-120 min against the 7200 s timeout. timeout_s raised to 10800 so a retry cannot time out on the same work; the run now prints one SE_WALKFORWARD_DAY progress line per test day. One-off job; nothing about the fits changes.
